overall: Atlanta has already experienced its daily high for June 22 — a running maximum of 91.4°F was reached at approximately 16:19-17:00 ET and has held steady through 22:49 ET while temperatures have since dropped to 78.8°F. The day ran notably warmer than all three NWP models predicted, driven by afternoon clearing (sky cover dropped to FEW by 15:52), strong solar heating, and a brief spike to 89.6°F at 14:52 that preceded the confirmed peak. No tropical or severe weather affected Atlanta; the active Flood Warnings are for the Satilla River in southeastern Georgia (Ware, Pierce, Brantley counties), well outside the metro area.
forecast_obs_notes: All three NWP models underforecast today's high — HRRR was closest at 90.1°F, while ECMWF (87.5°F) and NBM (86.8°F) were 3.9–4.6°F too cool. The observed 91.4°F running max exceeded even HRRR by 1.3°F, likely due to afternoon cloud clearing that outperformed model expectations. The INTRADAY model's 96.8% assignment to the 90–91°F bucket closely matches the confirmed observation, validating its obs-driven signal late in the day.
max_temp_prediction: Today's TMAX is effectively locked in at 91.4°F. There is negligible probability of any further warming tonight — the NWS forecast calls for a low around 72°F. Confidence in 91.4°F as the final TMAX is extremely high (~97%).
